60 Minutes is the longest-running primetime television program in American history. It's an investigative news magazine that debuted on CBS in 1968, and it fundamentally changed television journalism by bringing serious, in-depth reporting into the evening slots when people actually watched television. The show's format was three to four long-form investigative segments per episode, each anchored by correspondent personalities with their own distinctive styles. That format proved audiences would watch challenging journalism when it was told with compelling storytelling and professional production values.

The show premiered on CBS in September 1968 as an experiment in using the Sunday seven o'clock time slot for news rather than entertainment. Nobody knew if it would work, but it succeeded beyond anybody's expectations, and it's still on the air today. Don Hewitt, the legendary news producer, created it. He pioneered the magazine format itself and he insisted on maintaining journalistic rigor while employing cinematic visual techniques, which was a revolutionary combination at the time. The show featured a rotating roster of correspondents, most famously Mike Wallace, Morley Safer, Dan Rather, and Andy Rooney. Each brought distinctive interview styles and investigated different stories each week. Segments ranged from corporate malfeasance and political corruption to human-interest stories and international reporting, setting the standard for what investigative television journalism could be.

The show's opening, the iconic stopwatch ticking off the seconds, became one of television's most recognizable branding elements. It signaled the urgency and precision of the reporting. Andy Rooney's weekly essays became a cultural fixture, offering folksy commentary on modern life and frequently sparking national debate about the everyday absurdities of American life. The show won numerous Peabody and Emmy Awards and set the template for the news magazines that followed, like 20/20 and Dateline NBC, though 60 Minutes remained the ratings and cultural leader for decades.
